findings.title: Humanity as the stated barrier
findings.claim: 17:94 places the refusal after guidance has arrived and names the question of a human messenger as its stated barrier. Wider supplied passages keep that human role in two live settings: it is mocked or rejected (25:41, 64:6), and a human messenger can receive revelation or be sent among his people to recite and teach (18:110, 3:164). The matching post-arrival obstruction frame in 18:55 has a different stated condition.
findings.mechanism: The focus's negation-and-exception frame ties prevented belief to the quoted question; بشرًا supplies the human category and رسولًا the messenger role. The Arabic in 18:55 repeats the prevention-of-belief-after-guidance relation but gives a different exception. The supplied text of 25:41 sets a closely matching sending question in a mockery scene, while 64:6 links arriving messengers to the objection 'Will humans guide us?' and then to disbelief. In the other direction, 18:110 pairs human likeness with receiving revelation, and 3:164 presents a messenger from among the people reciting signs and teaching. Contact through the focus's barrier, human, and messenger words makes the human form the stated object of refusal while leaving the message-bearing capacity visible.
findings.reader_payoff: The question reads as a condition imposed on the kind of bearer who may bring guidance. The wider settings show both resistance to that human form and the work a human messenger receives and carries, so the focus describes a message refused after arrival.
findings.containment: The comparison does not establish direct borrowing, historical dependence, or one cause for every refusal; 18:55 states a different condition. The external connection rows supply target Arabic but no target morphology. In 25:41 the noun بشر is not repeated, so its link to the focus's explicit human descriptor remains a surface-level rhetorical inference.

epistemic.reason: The reader-walk nominations are legacy_unbound and non-citable; their bounded claim is checked against exact focus occurrences and exact target Arabic in the supplied connection rows. Missing target morphology limits the wider contacts to qualified surface-level comparisons.
